body: The landlord, HCJV 115 & 135 Hoyt Avenue Owner, LLC, leased a commercial unit in Mamaroneck to Project Veritas in 2020 for five years, from November 1, 2020 through October 31, 2025. Rent was due on the first of each month, payments more than 10 days late drew additional interest, and section 20 of the lease required any modification to be in writing and signed by the party against whom it would be enforced.

According to the decision, in December 2023 the tenant told the landlord it would need to terminate the lease that month and would be vacating. The landlord sent a lease termination agreement, which the tenant never signed or returned. The landlord sued in January 2024 for breach of the lease, and the tenant answered in March 2024 with affirmative defenses including estoppel. Supreme Court, Westchester County (Justice William J. Giacomo) granted the landlord summary judgment on December 20, 2024 and, after an inquest on damages, entered judgment on March 6, 2025 in the principal sum of $114,098.96.

The Second Department affirmed, with costs. Under General Obligations Law section 15-301(1), a contract that requires written modifications cannot be changed orally, unless part performance is "unequivocally referable" to the oral change. The tenant pointed to a "termination payment" covering rent due to date, forfeiture of its security deposit, and leaving behind its "desks, chairs and other office equipment." The court held that the rent payment and deposit forfeiture were what the lease itself provided for, and that leaving the furniture, which the tenant said without substantiation was worth thousands of dollars, was not unequivocally referable to a termination deal. The tenant therefore raised no triable issue on part performance or estoppel. The court did not reach the parties' remaining arguments.
